subject: science
name: Science
course: Forces, Motion, Life Cycles, Weather & Climates
title: Grade 3 Science: Forces, Motion, Life Cycles, Weather & Climates
overview: Grade 3 Science engages students in the scientific method and engineering design process across physical, life, and Earth/space sciences aligned with Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS).
competencies: Ask scientific questions, plan and conduct controlled investigations, and analyze experimental data.
Develop and use models to describe natural systems, energy flows, and physical interactions.
Construct explanations supported by empirical evidence and scientific reasoning.
Design, test, and optimize engineering solutions to real-world technological and environmental problems.

modules.title: Forces, Interactions & Magnetic Fields
modules.description: Investigating balanced and unbalanced forces, friction, predictive motion patterns, and non-contact magnetic forces.

topics.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
topics.description: Observing how equal and unequal forces affect the motion of carts and swings.

topics.title: Magnetic Forces and Static Electricity
topics.description: Testing north and south magnetic poles, magnetic fields, and designing magnetic locks.

modules.title: Life Cycles, Inherited Traits & Adaptations
modules.description: Comparing unique plant and animal life cycles, exploring trait inheritance and variation, and fossil evidence of past life.

topics.title: Diverse Life Cycles of Organisms
topics.description: Comparing life cycles of butterflies, frogs, flowering plants, and mammals.

topics.title: Inheritance, Environmental Traits & Variation
topics.description: Differentiating between genetic traits (eye color) and environmental influences (plant height).

topics.title: Fossils and Ancient Environments
topics.description: Analyzing fossilized teeth and shells to infer ancient environmental conditions.

modules.title: Weather, Climates & Natural Hazard Mitigation
modules.description: Analyzing world climate zones, seasonal weather data tables, and engineering designs to reduce severe weather damage.

topics.title: Weather Data Analysis Across Seasons
topics.description: Graphing daily temperature and precipitation tables to predict seasonal trends.

topics.title: World Climate Zones & Biomes
topics.description: Contrasting tropical, temperate, arid, and polar climate regions on Earth.

topics.title: Engineering Solutions for Severe Weather Hazards
topics.description: Designing lightning rods, storm shutters, and elevated flood barriers.
